about: Text of the printable in-car guide (one per vehicle, laminated, in the cubby hole). before/after rows: [title, text].
before: Look at the round disc on the inside of the windscreen. The date must not have passed.
Walk slowly all the way round. Look for new dents, scratches, cracks or broken lights. Take a photo of anything new before you leave, so you’re not blamed for it.
Look at all four tyres. Does one look flatter than the others? Any cuts, lumps or nails? If so, don’t drive: call the coordinator.
Look at the ground under the vehicle. A puddle of oil, coolant (green, pink or orange) or fuel means: don’t drive.
Every passenger needs a seat that has a working belt. Pull each belt quickly: it must lock. Click it in: it must hold.
Start the engine. All the dashboard lights should go out within a few seconds. A red light that stays on means: don’t drive.
Switch on the headlights and the hazards and walk round: every light should work. Ask someone to check the brake lights.
Check the warning triangle, jack, wheel spanner and spare wheel are in the vehicle.
Record the fuel level and the km reading when you sign the vehicle out.
road: A red warning light comes on
The temperature needle goes above the middle, or you see steam
Thick smoke from the exhaust, or a burning smell
The brakes grind, feel soft, or the vehicle pulls hard when braking
A tyre feels flat, or the vehicle wobbles or pulls
A loud new noise: knocking, grinding or banging
after: Look for any new damage and take photos of it. Report it honestly when you hand the vehicle back: accidents happen, hiding them causes bigger problems.
Look at all four tyres again for damage or a soft tyre.
Did any light come on during the trip, even for a moment? Tell the vehicle coordinator when you hand it back.
Remove all rubbish, food and personal things. Shake out the mats if they’re sandy.
Record the fuel level and the km reading when you hand the vehicle back.
Hand back every key, remote and the locknut key.
Tell the vehicle coordinator about anything that didn’t feel, sound or smell right, however small.
breakdown: Switch on the hazard lights and pull off the road as far as you safely can.
Everyone gets out on the side away from the traffic and waits behind a barrier or well off the road.
Put on the reflective vest. Place the warning triangle about 45 m behind the vehicle (about 60 big steps).
Call roadside assistance (number on the emergency card in the cubby hole), then the vehicle coordinator.
In an emergency call 112 from a cellphone, or 10111 for the police.
